scene_translation: You step out of Shinjuku Station's south exit into the flowing tide of people under the dusk light. You're checking your map, bag slung over your shoulder, when you notice a small envelope lying at your feet. Picking it up, you see written in an unfamiliar hand: 'To テスト-sama.' The old man standing beside you glances over and murmurs quietly, 'I've been waiting for you, テスト-san.'
grammar_note: 【〜のに気がつく】'to notice that ~' — のに here connects a verb clause to 気がつく, expressing the moment of realizing something. e.g. 封筒が落ちているのに気がついた = 'I noticed that an envelope was lying there.' Very useful for mystery and discovery moments.

vocab.meaning: honorific suffix, more formal than さん

mystery_memo: Central mystery: someone knew the player's name before they arrived in Tokyo and left a sealed envelope for them at Shinjuku Station's south exit. The old man also knows the player's name and claims to have been waiting — he is a key figure. The envelope is unopened and its contents are unknown. The player has just arrived, so no prior relationship has been established with any NPC yet.
